presentation.label: STRING
presentation.summary: A Karplus-Strong plucked string SRC machine: bowed, hit, noise or plucked strings that go through the Digitakt's own AMP, filter, mixer and effects.
presentation.overview: STRING adds a Karplus-Strong physical-model string to the SRC machine list of the original Digitakt. Choose an exciter (BOW, HIT, NOISE or PLUCK), then shape the string with stiffness, pluck position, softness, damping and a decay time. Machine Pages draws its SRC page with STRING's own names, ranges and defaults. It stores its values in SLICE's eight parameter slots, so they are saved with the project, can be locked per step and are reachable by MIDI CC and NRPN like any stock parameter. Its audio enters the normal AMP envelope, filter, mixer and sends.
highlights: Four exciters: BOW keeps exciting the string while the note is held; HIT, NOISE and PLUCK are one-shot.
DECAY is a time (T60, 0.07 s to about 17 s, endless at the top): the same setting rings as long on a low note as on a high one.
STIFF moves from an ideal string to a bell-like, inharmonic tone; TONE sets the damping inside the string.
Retriggering a ringing string adds the new excitation to the vibration, as on a real string.
Values are ordinary SLICE slots: saved, p-lockable, LFO destinations and MIDI CC/NRPN controllable.
usage: Select an audio track, press FUNC + SRC, choose STRING in the machine list and confirm with YES.
Play a trig key: the default sound is a plucked string at the track's pitch. Turn knob B (EXC) to choose BOW, HIT, NOISE or PLUCK, drawn as icons.
Turn knob H (DECAY) to set how long the string rings, and knob G (TONE) from 0 (warm) to 4 (open and metallic). The AMP page still shapes what you hear.
Return to a stock machine with FUNC + SRC; the track's SLICE values stay in the project.

access.location: SRC machine list (FUNC + SRC), as STRING
steps: Use a build containing STRING for the original Digitakt on OS 1.53 or 1.54.
Select an audio track, press FUNC + SRC, choose STRING in the machine list and confirm with YES.
The SRC page then shows TUNE, EXC, STIFF, POS, SOFT, TONE and DECAY; knob D is blank.

controls.name: A — TUNE
controls.doc: Pitch, with the stock range. An untransposed note plays C4 at 261.6 Hz; the keyboard follows equal temperament up to about 12 kHz.

controls.name: B — EXC
controls.doc: Exciter, drawn as an icon: BOW, HIT (mallet), NOISE or PLUCK; default PLUCK. BOW keeps exciting the string while the note is held; the others are one-shot.

controls.name: C — STIFF
controls.doc: Stiffness, 0–127: from an ideal string to a bell-like, inharmonic tone. The fundamental stays in tune up to about 880 Hz.

controls.name: D — (blank)
controls.doc: Blank: STRING plays no sample, so the sample selector is hidden.

controls.name: E — POS
controls.doc: Pluck position, OFF or 1–64, from the bridge to the middle of the string; default OFF.

controls.name: G — TONE
controls.doc: Damping inside the string, 0–4: 0 warm, 3 bright, 4 open and metallic. Its cutoff follows the note and rises with DECAY.

controls.name: H — DECAY
controls.doc: How long the string itself rings (T60), 0–127: 0.07 s to about 17 s, endless at the top. The AMP envelope decides how long you hear it.

controls.name: LFO destinations
controls.doc: The LFO destination list shows the STRING parameter names, grouped as STRG.

limitations: Below F#1 (47 Hz) the string runs at a lower internal rate, down to about 1.5 Hz, without octave jumps.
High STIFF values make very high notes slightly sharp (about +8 cents at 1760 Hz).
On high notes with a long DECAY the damping filter opens completely, so TONE 3 and 4 can sound the same there.
SOFT now spans 0–127; a sound saved with 0.8.0 keeps its stored value, so its attack is about half as soft as before.
Machine Pages conflicts with DigiChain, so STRING cannot be combined with Digi Mono or Digi Poly.

load.display: Three STRING tracks play cleanly on hardware; from four, the UI lags
load.conditions: Author's Digitakt I, OS 1.54, Core 2.1, Machine Pages 1.2 and STRING (builds M003 and M004), 2026-10-28, judged by ear and by the UI's response. With digihealth (M005) the DSP load reads 81, 87, 91, 95, 96 and 98% for one to six tracks, within 3 points of STRING 0.8.0 on the same pattern (M006), which also lags from four tracks. The count depends on the sounds: long DECAY, BOW and low notes cost more.

hardware.summary: Alez22 flashed the Modwerk-compiled STRING 0.9.0 with Core 2.1, Machine Pages 1.2, RAM Machines 1.3.1 and Note Accumulator 1.1.1 (build M003) on OS 1.53 (5 minutes) and OS 1.54 (15 minutes): STRING appears in the machine list with its icon, its SRC page shows its names, EXC icons and a blank knob D, its own defaults apply when a track switches to STRING, LFO destinations are grouped as STRG, a project survives save, power cycle and reload, Note Accumulator transposes STRING, and RAM Machines records and plays back STRING. Three STRING tracks play cleanly; from four the UI lags, as with 0.8.0 on the same pattern.
limitations: Track count measured on OS 1.54 only.
DSP readout taken with digihealth in separate builds (M005, M006); digihealth is not part of this module.
Tested SysEx: 1.53 73d4f1f3924c90c7114e60d1d89be86647a9cb08fe80514bf072c4670cf2148f, 1.54 ef1a7631d27e832888edc34d21c61fcbc5b5ecd69a7710928f93c82c509256ed. Firmware was not read back from the device.
A project saved with 0.8.0 was loaded unchanged on the author's elekloader builds of the same source (Core 4.1, Machine Pages 1.5), not on M003.

tests.summary: Hardware (author, OS 1.53 and 1.54, 20 min, with Machine Pages, RAM Machines and Note Accumulator): machine list, SRC page, defaults, LFO, save/reboot/reload, Note Accumulator and RAM Machines work; three tracks clean, the UI lags from four, at the same DSP load as 0.8.0. Source-only packages compiled in the pinned toolchain; emulator captures on OS 1.53 and 1.54 are identical.
